entities.summary: Condoleezza "Condi" Rice is an American diplomat and political scientist who served as the 66th United States secretary of state from 2005 to 2009 and as the 19th U.S. national security advisor from 2001 to 2005. Since 2020, she has served as the 8th director of Stanford University's Hoover Institution. A member of the Republican Party, Rice was the first female African-American secretary of state and the first woman to serve as national security advisor. Until the election of Barack Obama as president in 2008, Rice and her predecessor, Colin Powell, were the highest-ranking African Americans in the history of the federal executive branch.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first female African-American secretary of state and national security advisor, Condoleezza Rice played a pivotal role in shaping U.S. foreign policy during a critical period, particularly in the aftermath of 9/11 and the Iraq War.
